problem: The chapter defines transit time as "the spread in electron arrival times at the anode". Transit time itself is the average time an electron takes to travel from the photocathode to the anode. The spread of those times is a separate quantity, transit-time spread (or jitter). Students will confuse the two and write the wrong definition in the exam.
fix: Transit time is the average time an electron takes to travel from the photocathode to the anode. The spread in these arrival times, called transit-time spread, limits timing resolution; the finite pulse width and the dead time limit the count rate.

problem: "Detects radiation that does not make enough light by itself" is vague: a student may read "by itself" as referring to the counter rather than the radiation.
fix: A scintillation counter detects radiation that produces too little light on its own to be sensed directly, so a scintillator first converts the radiation into a light flash.
